subject.title: [Feature]: Support arbitrary workspace files in bootstrap context injection

question: Should OpenClaw accept explicitly configured custom-basename bootstrap files as a core hook contract, and should that contract be global-only or exact-session scoped as proposed in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/74735?
rationale: This is feasible in code, but it changes deterministic prompt context, file-loading scope, and user-facing hook configuration semantics, which repository policy treats as product and compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Approve Repaired Hook Contract
options.body: Allow custom-basename files through the existing bootstrap-extra-files path after the linked PR or a replacement preserves path guards, budgets, filtering, and clear docs.

options.title: Narrow To Global Extras
options.body: Accept arbitrary explicitly configured global paths while deferring exact session-key selectors to a separate design.

options.title: Keep Recognized Basenames
options.body: Reject arbitrary bootstrap injection for now and steer users toward first-class bootstrap files or manual workspace conventions.

recommendation.title: Approve Repaired Hook Contract
recommendation.body: Allow custom-basename files through the existing bootstrap-extra-files path after the linked PR or a replacement preserves path guards, budgets, filtering, and clear docs.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the original hook work and later refactored the same boundary-safe bootstrap read path, making them the strongest decision-routing signal from history.
